journal.case: Charmaine Hamer, Petitioner v. Neighborhood Housing Services of Chicago, et al. Arugued by Mr. Jonathan A. Herstoff for the petitioner and by Mr. Damien G. Stewart for the respondents. Adjourned until Wednesday, October 11, 2017, at 10 o’clock. Certiorari—Summary Disposition

Donald J. Trump, President of the United States, et al., Petitioners v. International Refugee Assistance, et al. We granted certiorari in this case to resolve a challenge to “the temporary suspension of entry of aliens abroad under Section 2(c) of Executive Order No. 13,780.” Because that provision of the Order “expired by its own terms” on September 24, 2017
journal.text: the appeal no longer presents a “live case or controversy.” Burke v. Barnes, 479 U. S. 361, 363 (1987). Following our established practice in such cases, the judgment is therefore vacated, and the case is remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit with instructions to dismiss as moot the challenge to Executive Order No. 13,780. United States v. Munsing­ wear, Inc., 340 U. S. 36, 39 (1950). We express no view on the merits. Justice Sotomayor dissents from the order vacating the judgment below And would dismiss the writ of certiorari as improvidently granted.

journal.case: Jefferson S. Dunn, Commissioner, Alabama Department of Corrections, et al., Applicants v. Torrey Twane McNabb. Application to vacate the injunction entered by the United States District Court for the Middle District of Alabama on October 16, 2017, presented to Justice Thomas and by him referred to the Court, is granted. “[I]nmates seeking time to challenge the manner in which the State plans to execute them must satisfy all of the requirements for a stay, including a showing of a signiﬁcant possibility of success on the merits.” Hill v. McDonough, 547 U. S. 573, 584 (2006). The All Writs Act does not excuse a court from making these ﬁndings. Because the District Court enjoined respondent’s execution without ﬁnding that he has a signiﬁ- cant possibility of success on the merits, it abused its discretion. We accordingly vacate the injunction. Justice Breyer and Justice Sotomayor would deny
journal.text: the application to vacate the injunction. Certiorari Denied

journal.case: Donald J. Trump, President of the United States, et al., Petitioners v. Hawaii, et al. We granted certiorari in this case to resolve a challenge to the temporary suspension of entry of aliens and refugees under Section 2(c) and Section 6 of Executive Order No. 13,780. Because those provisions of the Order have “expired by [their] own terms,”
journal.text: the appeal no longer presents a “live case or controversy.” Burke v. Barnes, 479 U. S. 361, 363 (1987). Following our established practice in such cases, the judgment is therefore vacated, and the case is remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit with instructions to dismiss as moot the challenge to Executive Order No. 13,780. United States v. Munsingwear, Inc., 340 U. S. 36, 39 (1950). We express no view on the merits. Justice Sotomayor dissents from the order vacating the judgment below and would dismiss the writ of certiorari as improvidently granted.

journal.case: In Re David Pannell, Petitioner.
journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of mandamus and/or prohibition dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court’s process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Co­ lumbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam). Rehearings Denied

journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of certiorari to the District Court of Appeal of Florida, Fourth District dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court’s process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

journal.case: Donald J. Trump, President of the United States, et al., Applicants v. Hawaii, et al.
journal.text: The application for a stay presented to Justice Kennedy and by him referred to the Court is granted, and the District Court’s October 20, 2017 order granting a preliminary injunction is stayed pending disposition of the Government’s appeal in the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit and disposition of the Government’s petition for a writ of certiorari, if such writ is sought. If a writ of certiorari is sought and the Court denies the petition, this order shall terminate automatically. If the Court grants the petition for a writ of certiorari, this order shall terminate when the Court enters its judgment. In light of its decision to consider the case on an expedited basis, we expect that the Court of Appeals will render its decision with appropriate dispatch. Justice Ginsburg and Justice Sotomayor would deny the application. Order in Pending Case
journal.case: Donald J. Trump, President of the United States, et al., Applicants v. International Refugee Assistance Project, et al.
journal.text: The application for a stay presented to The Chief Justice and by him referred to the Court is granted, and the District Court’s October 17, 2017 order granting a preliminary injunction is stayed pending disposition of the Government’s appeal in the United State Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit and disposition of the Government’s petition for a writ of certiorari, if such writ is sought. If a writ of certiorari is sought and the Court denies the petition, this order shall terminate automatically. If the Court grants the petition for a writ of certiorari, this order shall terminate when the Court enters its judgment. In light of its decision to consider the case on an expedited basis, we expect that the Court of Appeals will render its decision with appropriate dispatch. Justice Ginsburg and Justice Sotomayor would deny the application.

journal.case: Antonneo R. Boyce, Petitioner v. Arizona.
journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for a writ of certiorari to the Court of Appeals of Arizona, Division One dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court’s process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

journal.text: On petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit. Motion to proceed in forma pauperis and petition for writ of certiorari are granted. Judgment vacated, and case remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit for further consideration of the question whether Tharpe is entitled to a Certiﬁcate of Appealability. Justice Thomas, with whom Justice Alito and Justice Gorsuch join, dissenting. Opinion per curiam. Certiorari—Summary Dispositions
journal.case: Amy Sanders, Petitioner v. Lamar Jones.
journal.text: On petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit. Petition for writ of certiorari granted. Judgment vacated, and case remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit for further consideration in light of Manuel v. Joliet, 580 U. S. __ (2017).

journal.text: On petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit. Petition for writ of certiorari granted. journal.case: Nathanael Lenard Reynolds, Petitioner v. South Carolina, et al
Nathanael Lenard Reynolds, Petitioner v. South Carolina, et al.
journal.text: Motions of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petitions for writs of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court’s process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of certiorari to the Court of Appeals of Colorado dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court's process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Co­ lumbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

journal.text: Argued by Mr. Gregory G. Garre for the plaintiff, by Mr. Craig S. Primis for the defendant, and by Mr. Edwin S. Kneedler for the United States as amicus curiae, by special leave of the Court, in support of overruling Florida’s exception 2c. Adjourned until Tuesday, January 9, 2018, at 10 o’clock.

journal.case: Jon Husted, Ohio Secretary of State, Petitioner v. A. Philip Randolph Institute, et al.
journal.text: Argued by Mr. Eric E. Murphy for the petitioner, by Mr. Solicitor General Noel J. Francisco for the United States as amicus curiae, by special leave of the Court, supporting the petitioner, and by Mr. Paul M. Smith for the respondents. The Chief Justice said: “You can have a couple of minutes.” Argument continued by Mr. Paul M. Smith for the respondents, and by Mr. Eric E. Murphy for the petitioner, to whom The Chief Justice allotted 5 additional minutes. Adjourned until Tuesday, January 16, 2018, at 10 o’clock.

journal.text: Application for stay of execution of sentence of death presented to Justice Thomas and by him referred to the Court granted pending the disposition of the petition for writ of certiorari. Should the petition for writ of certiorari be denied, this stay shall terminate automatically. Justice Thomas, Justice Alito, and Justice Gorsuch would deny the application.

journal.text: On writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. Judgment afﬁrmed. Justice Thomas announced the judgment of the Court and delivered an opinion in which Justice Breyer, Justice Alito, and Justice Kagan joined. Concurring opinion by Justice Breyer. Opinion concurring in the judgment by Justice Ginsburg, with whom Justice Sotomayor joins. Opinion concurring in the judgment by Justice Sotomayor. Dissenting opinion by The Chief Justice, with whom Justice Kennedy and Justice Gorsuch join.
journal.case: David Jennings, et al., Petitioners v. Alejandro Rodriguez, et al., Individually and on Behalf of All Others Similarly Situated.
journal.text: On writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. Judgment reversed and case remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. Justice Alito delivered the opinion of the Court, except as to Part II. Opinion by Justice Thomas, with whom Justice Gorsuch joins except for footnote 6, concurring in part and concurring in the judgment. Dissenting opinion announced by Justice Breyer, with whom Justice Ginsburg and Justice Sotomayor join. Justice Kagan took no part in the decision of this case.

journal.case: Joel Christopher Holmes, Petitioner v. Don Kennedy Properties, LLC.
journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of certiorari dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court’s process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

journal.case: (17A911). Russell Bucklew, Petitioner v. Anne L. Precythe, Director, Missouri Department of Corrections, et al.
journal.text: Application for stay of execution of sentence of death presented to Justice Gorsuch and by him referred to the Court is granted pending the disposition of the petition for a writ of certiorari. Should the petition for a writ of certiorari be denied, this stay shall terminate automatically. In the event the petition for a writ of certiorari is granted, the stay shall terminate upon the sending down of the judgment of this Court. The Chief Justice, Justice Thomas, Justice Alito, and Justice Gorsuch would deny the application for stay of execution.

journal.case: Jefferson B. Sessions, III, Attorney General, Petitioner v. James Garcia Dimaya.
journal.text: On writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. Judgment afﬁrmed. Justice Kagan announced the judgment of the Court and delivered an opinion of the Court with respect to Parts I, III, IV–B, and V, and an opinion with respect to Parts II and IV–A, in which Justice Ginsburg, Justice Breyer, and Justice Sotomayor join. Opinion by Justice Gorsuch concurring in part and concurring in the judgment. Dissenting opinion by The Chief Justice, with whom Justice Kennedy, Justice Thomas, and Justice Alito join. Dissenting opinion by Justice Thomas, with whom Justice Kennedy and Justice Alito join as to Parts I–C–2, II–A–1, and II–B.

Opinion per curiam announced by The Chief Justice. journal.case: Masoud Bamdad, Petitioner v. United States.
journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court’s process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

journal.case: Charles Pointer, Petitioner v. Allied Barton Security Company.
journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court’s process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam).

journal.text: On writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit. Judgment of the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit in No. 16–285 reversed, and case remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Seventh Cir­ cuit for further proceedings consistent with the opinion of this Court. Judgment of the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit in No. 16–300 reversed, and case remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit for further proceedings consistent with the opinion of this Court. Judgment of the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit in No. 16-307 afﬁrmed. Opinion by Justice Gorsuch. Concurring opinion by Justice Thomas. Dissenting opinion announced by Justice Ginsburg, with whom Justice Breyer, Justice Sotomayor, and Justice Kagan join.

journal.case: Alex M. Azar, II, Secretary of Health and Human Services, et al., Petitioners v. Rochelle Garza, as Guardian ad Litem to Unaccompanied Minor J. D.
journal.text: On petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit. Motion of petitioners to lodge non-record material under seal with redacted copies for the public record granted. Petition for writ of certiorari granted. The Court vacates the en banc order and remands the case to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit with instructions to direct the District Court to dismiss the relevant individual claim for injunctive relief as moot. See United States v. Munsingwear, Inc., 340 U. S. 36 (1950). Opinion per curiam. Appeal—Summary Disposition

journal.case: In Re Dean Carbajal, Petitioner.
journal.text: Motion of petitioner for leave to proceed in forma pauperis denied, and petition for writ of habeas corpus dismissed. See Rule 39.8. As petitioner has repeatedly abused this Court’s process, the Clerk is directed not to accept any further petitions in noncriminal matters from petitioner unless the docketing fee required by Rule 38(a) is paid and petition submitted in compliance with Rule 33.1. See Martin v. District of Columbia Court of Appeals, 506 U. S. 1 (1992) (per curiam). Mandamus Denied

journal.case: Florida, Plaintiff v. Georgia. On Exceptions to Report of the Special Master. Case remanded.
journal.text: Opinion by Justice Breyer. Dissenting opinion by Justice Thomas, with whom Justice Alito, Justice Kagan, and Justice Gorsuch join. The Chief Justice said: “I am authorized to announce that the Court has acted upon all cases submitted to the Court for decision this Term. Disposition of items scheduled for conference today will be reﬂected on an order list that will be released at 9:30 tomorrow morning. The Court will be in recess from today until the ﬁrst Monday in October 2018, at which time the October 2017 Term of the Court will be adjourned, and the October 2018 Term of the Court will begin, as provided by law.” “On behalf of my colleagues, I would like to thank the Supreme Court employees for their outstanding work and dedication to their important responsibilities during this Term. The commitment and pro­ fessionalism of all the Court staff contribute signiﬁcantly to the accom­ plishment of the Court’s mission. The Court also thanks the members of the Court’s Bar for their professionalism and cooperation.” “Before we rise for the summer, I would like to note the retirement of three Court employees. Corporal John Gilliam has announced his retirement, effective June 30 of this year. Corporal Gilliam has served with distinction and retires with 20 years of outstanding service on the Supreme Court police force. Cristi Cherry, a paralegal specialist and secretary to our Legal Counsel, is retiring on June 29 of this year with 23 years of Supreme Court service. We are grateful for her many contributions to the Legal Counsel’s ofﬁce. Finally, my administrative assistant, Diane Nelson, has announced she is retiring July 12, with 12 years of Supreme Court service. I am personally grateful to Diane for her dedication, hard work, and friendship. Corporal Gilliam, Ms. Cherry, and Ms. Nelson, the Court thanks each of you for your service, and we wish you well in your retirement.” Adjourned until Monday, October 1, 2018, at 10 o’clock. Certiorari Denied

journal.case: United States, et al., Applicants v. United States District Court for the District of Oregon.
journal.text: The application for stay presented to Justice Kennedy and by him referred to the Court denied. The Government’s request for relief is premature and is denied with­ out prejudice. The breadth of respondents’ claims is striking, however, and the justiciability of those claims presents substantial grounds for difference of opinion. The District Court should take these concerns into account in assessing the burdens of discovery and trial, as well as the desirability of a prompt ruling on the Government’s pending dispositive motions.

The order en­ tered June 28, 2018, denying the petition for writ of certiorari vacated as to petitioner Michael Biggs. Petition for writ of certiorari as to Mi­ chael Biggs granted. Judgment vacated, and case remanded to the United States Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces for further con­ sideration in light of United States v. Mangahas, 77 M. J. 220 (2018). Food Marketing Institute, Applicant v. Argus Leader Media, dba Argus Leader. Application to recall and stay the mandate, presented to Justice Gorsuch and by him referred to the Court, is granted, and the mandate of the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit in case No. 17–1346 is recalled and stayed pending the timely ﬁling and disposition of
journal.text: a petition for a writ of certiorari. Should the petition for a writ of certiorari be denied, this stay shall terminate automatically. In the event the petition for a writ of certio­ rari is granted, the stay shall terminate upon the sending down of the judgment of this Court. Justice Ginsburg, Justice Sotomayor, and Justice Kagan would deny the application.

journal.text: Application for injunctive relief presented to Justice Alito and by him referred to the Court denied. Justice Thomas, Justice Alito, and Justice Gorsuch would grant the application.

journal.text: motion of respondents for divided argument denied. Motion of respondent Jason D. Sims for appointment of counsel granted, and Jeffrey L. Fisher, of Stanford, California, is appointed to serve as counsel for respondent Jason D. Sims in No. 17–766.
journal.case: Florida, Plaintiff v. Georgia. The August 9, 2018, Order in this case is amended to provide that the compensation of a legal assistant for the Special Master shall be charged against and borne by the parties in such proportion as the Court may hereafter direct. The cost of printing the Special Master's Reports, and all other proper expenses, including travel expenses, shall be submitted to the Court
Gary Thacker, et ux., Petitioners v. Tennessee Valley Authority.
journal.text: Petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit granted.
journal.case: Home Depot U. S. A., Inc., Petitioner v. George W. Jackson.
journal.text: Petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit granted. In addition to the questions presented by the petition, the parties are directed to brief and argue the following question: Should this Court's holding in Shamrock Oil & Gas Corp. v. Sheets, 313 U. S. 100 (1941)—that an original plaintiff may not remove a counterclaim against it—extend to third-party counterclaim defendants?
journal.case: Alex M. Azar, II, Secretary of Health and Human Services, Petitioner v. Allina Health Services, et al.
journal.text: Petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit granted limited to the following question: Whether 42 U. S. C. § 1395hh(a)(2) or § 1395hh(a)(4) required the Department of Health and Human Services to conduct notice-and-comment rulemaking before providing the challenged instructions to a Medicare Administrator Contractor making initial determinations of payments due under Medicare.

journal.text: Petition for writ of certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit granted. Justice Alito took no part in the consideration or decision of this petition.
